prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: transparent standing-cardinal game-character source sheet
Primary request: Create one new ordinary clinic patient in everyday civilian clothes. Image1 controls only accepted v6a/v6b rounded pixel-art style and proportional scale, not its identity or clothes.
Subject: a 88-year-old adult woman with deep dark-brown skin, fine straight silver hair in a short smooth side-swept crop, small round pearl earrings and no glasses; one dark-brown cane with a cream curved handle held in the left hand as a visual mobility aid, and a sturdy build. They wear a pale-lilac full-sleeved cardigan over a pale-yellow blouse, a cream calf-length skirt and navy slip-on shoes. All sleeves are full length to the wrists. No badge, lanyard, scrubs or white coat. Calm friendly expression, right arm relaxed at the side, left hand holding the cane.
Composition/framing: exactly four isolated full-body standing figures in one horizontal row, left-to-right SOUTH/front, EAST/true profile facing screen-right, WEST/true profile facing screen-left, NORTH/rear. Same identity, face, hair, outfit, head and body scale across all four views. Every head and shoe fully visible, with broad transparent gutters and outer margins.
Style/medium: compact rounded proportions, large expressive head, crisp softly shaded pixel art and clean dark pixel-stepped outline matching Image1.
Constraints: genuine transparent RGBA background. No hat, chair, furniture, floor, cast shadow, glow, props other than the described cane, devices, scenery, text, readable badge, logo, watermark, collage, grid, extra people, varied poses or cropped limbs.

Age and dignity: this is visibly a 88-year-old older adult, not a young person with recolored hair. Preserve the accepted rounded game proportions and large eyes, while using subtle crow's-feet, gentle cheek and mouth lines, age-appropriate hair density, and a gently forward but balanced relaxed posture. Warm, capable, calm expression; no caricature, frailty stereotype or exaggerated wrinkles. Appearance and accessories have no diagnostic meaning.
No eyeglasses in any view. Keep the specified hair silhouette, not the reference's gray curls; do not copy its rose cardigan, sage trousers or identity.
Mobility-aid continuity: a single simple dark-brown cane with cream curved handle remains in the anatomical LEFT hand in every view, its tip on the same floor line as the shoes. In seated views it stays upright beside the left knee. South/front: SCREEN RIGHT. North/rear: SCREEN LEFT. The true west profile may occlude it. Do not duplicate it or switch hands. The cane is visual only and is not tied to a diagnosis.
